question.text: An active FI manager with a 'rate-anticipation' approach primarily manipulates which portfolio characteristic?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes the interest-rate driven active strategy as managing portfolio duration based on forecasts of interest-rate fluctuations: duration is reduced when rates are expected to rise and increased when rates are expected to decline. The Trap: Sector allocation, credit ratings, and currency mix are other active levers, but they are not the "rate-anticipation" lever; rate anticipation operates specifically through portfolio duration. Note: Page 343 sets out the duration-based active rate-anticipation framework.
